title: South Korea's LG AI Research Opens 'K-Exaone 2.5' API Free to All, Partners with Nvidia
summary: LG AI Research releases K-Exaone 2.5 API for free in partnership with Nvidia
detailed: South Korea's LG AI Research made the API for its 'K-Exaone 2.5' foundation model free of charge to all developers, startups, and research institutions.
The model scored 74.6 on Automation Bench, 77.3 on ClawEval, 78.0 on BrowseComp, and 59.2 on SWE-Bench Pro in internal evaluations.
LG AI Research plans to use data design and reinforcement-learning techniques validated by this release to build its third-generation K-Exaone 3.0 model.
The company is also reviewing Nvidia's 'Dynamo' infrastructure technology to improve inference efficiency and service scalability.
This matters because providing a frontier-level South Korean foundation model without a paywall encourages local adoption and helps LG refine its training methodology.
sentences: South Korea's LG AI Research has fully opened the application programming interface (API) of "K-Exaone 2.5," its in-house artificial intelligence (AI) foundation model, free of charge.
The strategy is to refine the model through real-world use while securing the technological capability to compete with the world's top-tier AI models.
LG AI Research announced the plan on Nov.
9 at Nvidia AI Day Seoul 2026, held at COEX in Seoul's Gangnam district.

Starting that day, anyone — developers, startups, ordinary companies and research institutions — can obtain an API key through the Exaone website and use K-Exaone 2.5 for service development and research.
An API serves as a channel that connects outside programs or services so they can call up the functions of an AI model.
The release follows the intent of the "independent AI foundation model" development program pushed by South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT.
Ahead of developing a new model, it focused on refining the company's own training methodology and confirming where performance could be improved.
In particular, it is seen as having proven its competitiveness in the so-called "agentic AI" area, where AI sets its own plans and mobilizes external tools to handle tasks.
According to LG AI Research's own evaluation results, K-Exaone 2.5 scored 74.6 on "Automation Bench," which measures task-automation capability.
That is effectively on par with China's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (74.9) and ahead of GLM 5.3 (71.6).
On "ClawEval," which gauges AI agents' problem-solving in work environments, it scored 77.3, beating DeepSeek (75.8) and trailing GLM (77.6) by a narrow margin.

On "BrowseComp," which assesses web-browsing ability, it scored 78.0 to top DeepSeek (75.8), and on "SWE-Bench Pro," which measures software development and modification capability, it posted 59.2, higher than DeepSeek (58.4).
Note: Based on LG AI Research's own evaluation.
No numerical score for GLM 5.3 on SWE-Bench Pro is given in public materials; only a comparison confirming it is higher than K-Exaone 2.5 could be verified.

The idea is to transplant the proprietary training technology proven with K-Exaone 2.5 — across the entire process from data design to training, including data quality management, post-training and reinforcement learning — into the development of K-Exaone 3.0, completing a foundation model with global competitiveness.
Technology cooperation with Nvidia will proceed in parallel.
LG AI Research is reviewing adoption of Nvidia's "Dynamo" technology to raise the inference efficiency and service scalability of its AI models.

Dynamo is an infrastructure technology that distributes large-scale AI inference workloads to lower the cost of running services, and could help reduce cost burdens if usage rises after the model is opened free.

With a South Korean-made foundation model touting frontier-level performance released without a paywall, startups and research institutions burdened by API costs now have an incentive to apply it first to their own services and experiments.
For LG, a practical benefit is the ability to secure large volumes of real-world usage data for training and improving the 3.0 model.
Still, the inference cost burden of offering the model free and price and performance competition with the Chinese open-source camp, including DeepSeek and GLM, remain challenges ahead.
